findings.title: Standardized testing hack exposes names and addresses of millions of students - Los Angeles Times
findings.summary_md: The LA Times reported on October 16 that hackers stole records of millions of current and former California public school students through a breach at testing provider ETS. The exposed data includes names, addresses, demographic details and disability status, affecting students enrolled over the past three school years. The article attributes the incident to a compromised login used against an ETS secure file transfer site.

findings.title: California Department of Education Student Data Breach via ETS - GalaxyWarden
findings.summary_md: GalaxyWarden documented the ETS breach on October 16, noting that ETS notified families of unauthorized access to an SFTP site used by the California Department of Education. The breach exposed records spanning millions of students, including personal and disability information. The post confirms the incident involved a contractor rather than a direct CDE system compromise.

findings.title: Educational Testing Service (ETS) Notification - California Department of Education
findings.summary_md: The California Department of Education posted an ETS notification on October 16 describing unauthorized access and copying of student data from an ETS SFTP site. CDE distributed the notice to help affected individuals receive information about available resources. The advisory confirms the vendor is ETS and that millions of student records are involved.
